alarm-history.title: Recent alarms
announce.cleared: Announcement cleared. The banner is gone.
announce.dismissible-hint: Off by default, so everyone sees the notice until it ends or is taken down. On, each user can close it, and it stays closed for them until the notice is changed.
announce.empty-preview: Nothing to show yet. Write the notice below.
announce.empty-takes-down: Empty. Saving now takes the current notice down.
announce.ended: This announcement ended at {date} and is no longer shown. Save it with a new end, or turn the end off, to show it again.
announce.ends-hint: The bar disappears on its own at this time. Type the date (YYYY-MM-DD) or pick it on the calendar, then type the time (HH:mm, 24-hour) in your browser's time zone.
announce.ends-past: Pick a time in the future.
announce.hint: Shown to every signed-in user as a bar across the top of every page outside Admin. Delete all the text and save to take it down.
announce.preview-hint: The bar exactly as users will see it at the top of every page outside Admin, redrawn as you type.
announce.saved: Announcement saved. It shows on every workspace page.
announce.title: Announcement
announce.write-hint: The notice in Markdown: headings, **bold**, `code`, lists, links and :emoji: shortcodes, up to 1,000 characters.
approval.bulk-description: Approve a repository's entire pending queue in one action. Turn on "Approve only Clean packages" to approve just the packages with no known advisories and leave the rest pending.
approval.clean-only-hint: Approve and cache only packages whose scan found no known advisories. Vulnerable and unscanned packages stay pending for individual review.
approval.cvss-help: This is the CVSS version 3.x base score, which ranges from 0 to 10 and is calculated from the advisory's CVSS vector. A higher number means a more severe vulnerability. A score of 9.0 or above is critical, 7.0 or above is high, 4.0 or above is medium, and anything above 0 is low.
approval.deny-version-hint: Blocks one exact version even when the package is approved. Applies immediately, including already-cached copies.
approval.description: Review quarantined package requests across proxy and hosted repositories.
approval.no-approvers: No users currently have approve permission for this repository.
approval.no-queue: No repository currently has pending requests.
approval.not-scanned: Not scanned yet. The scan runs asynchronously after the request is queued; reload in a moment.
approval.queue-description: Quarantine queue for proxied and uploaded packages. Approve or reject requests before artifacts are served.
approval.read-only: You have read-only (auditor) access. Approval actions are disabled.
approval.rule-allow-note: Pre-approves the whole package: the first request is served without waiting in the queue.
approval.rule-block-note: Blocks the whole package, including already-cached content.
approval.rule-block-version-note: Blocks only this exact version; other versions of the package keep flowing.
approval.title: Approvals
approval.version-optional: Version (optional — leave empty to block the whole package)
approval.version-unknown: unknown (metadata request blocked before a version was resolved)
common.invalid-regex: Invalid regular expression. Results keep the last valid search until the pattern is fixed.
common.name: Name
common.name-rule: Letters, digits, dash and underscore only.
common.no-search-matches: No rows match the current search.
common.search-all-columns: Search all columns, wrap /pattern/ for regex
coverage.alarm-hint: After each scheduled scan, the projects still to migrate are posted to the receivers selected here.
coverage.alarm-preview-sample: No scan has completed yet, so this preview uses example numbers.
coverage.ci-hint: Whether the project's CI pipeline runs its build through forklift.
coverage.cron-hint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. For example 0 10 * * 1-5 is weekdays at 10:00.
coverage.description: How much of the organisation's source actually builds through forklift, measured by scanning each GitLab project's CI and package-manager configuration.
coverage.disabled: Coverage scanning is turned off. Set coverage.gitlab.enabled to true in the chart, or FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_ENABLED=true, to turn it on.
coverage.exclude-topics-hint: Comma separated GitLab topics. A repository carrying one opts itself out without a change here.
coverage.fill-required: Fill in the required fields before saving.
coverage.forklift-host-hint: The external domain a project's configuration must reference to count as wired. Defaults to the server's external URL, so most deployments leave it empty.
coverage.gitlab-missing: No GitLab instance is configured, so nothing can be scanned. Set FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_GITLAB_URL and FORKLIFT_COVERAGE_GITLAB_TOKEN.
coverage.gitlab-unreachable: The GitLab connection is not working
coverage.host-defaulted: Empty uses the server's own external URL.
coverage.host-missing: The forklift host is not set and the server has no external URL, so no project can match. Set one in the coverage settings.
coverage.host-no-dns: DNS did not resolve from forklift. Fine if your builds resolve it elsewhere.
coverage.host-not-bare: enter a bare domain, with no scheme, path or wildcard
coverage.host-not-external: not an external domain, so no build can resolve it
coverage.host-too-long: too long for a host name
coverage.max-branches-hint: How many branches besides the default one are searched for wiring.
coverage.mute-scopes-hint: A muted check is not required for the verdict and is not credited to it. Muting both takes the project out of coverage entirely.
coverage.muted-banner: This project is muted, so nothing below counts towards coverage.
coverage.muted-by-console: Muted from the console; use Unmute to bring it back.
coverage.muted-scopes-banner: These checks are muted, so the verdict below does not ask for them.
coverage.no-groups: No groups yet. Run a scan to see the breakdown.
coverage.no-pipeline-files: No GitLab CI files on this ref.
coverage.not-in-last-scan: The last scan produced no verdict for this project, either because it was excluded at the time or because it was created since.
coverage.project-not-found: That project could not be found.
coverage.receiver-hint: The report is posted to this receiver's webhook. Leave it empty and no report is sent.
coverage.registry-hint: Whether the project pulls its dependencies and base images from forklift.
coverage.scope-hint: What counts as forklift, and how far into each project the scan looks. Which projects are visible at all is decided by the GitLab access token.
coverage.send-report: Send a report after each scheduled scan
coverage.settings-description: What gets scanned, when, and where the report is sent. The GitLab connection itself comes from the environment.
coverage.since-days-hint: Branches with no commit in this window are not searched.
coverage.skip-when-full: Skip the report at full coverage
coverage.skip-when-full-hint: A report nobody has to act on is noise. A manual send still goes out.
coverage.timezone-freeform: Not in the list. Any IANA timezone name can be typed here.
coverage.timezone-hint: Pick one, or type any IANA name. The cron expression is read in this zone.
coverage.title: Forklift coverage
coverage.trend-empty: No trend yet. History builds up one point per scan.
coverage.unavailable: Coverage is not available on this forklift.
coverage.use-search-hint: Answers for the default branch in one call, but runs on a much lower rate limit than the ordinary API.
ha.description: Review storage topology, leader election state, and fencing token for the active cluster.
ha.failover-note: Manual failover gracefully steps this leader down so a standby is elected and takes over. The leader releases its lease and traffic moves to the new leader. This pod stays Ready and can be re-elected later. Use it for planned maintenance or to drain this pod. Expect a brief in-flight disruption while traffic moves.
ha.step-down-confirm-message: This leader gracefully releases its lease and a standby is elected. Traffic moves to the new leader. Expect a brief disruption. This pod stays Ready and can be re-elected later.
ha.stepping-down-notice: Stepping down - a standby is taking over. Traffic follows the new leader.
ha.title: HA Status
insight.admin-sprawl.action: Move day-to-day work to scoped roles (read, write, approve, security per repository pattern) and keep admin for break-glass accounts.
insight.admin-sprawl.criteria: Yellow: more than 3 enabled accounts hold the admin action on every repository (pattern *).
insight.admin-sprawl.summary: {count} active accounts hold admin on every repository (guideline: at most {limit}).
insight.admin-sprawl.summary-one: 1 active account holds admin on every repository (guideline: at most {limit}).
insight.admin-sprawl.title: Too many global administrators
insight.admin-sprawl.why: Every global administrator can change any policy, delete any repository and read every artifact. Each extra account is one more credential that can do all of that.
insight.age-policy-off.action: Enable the age policy (for example 3 days) so a hijacked or malicious release is usually pulled upstream before builds can fetch it.
insight.age-policy-off.criteria: Yellow: a proxy repository has the age policy off.
insight.age-policy-off.summary: {count} proxy repositories serve a version the moment it is published upstream.
insight.age-policy-off.summary-one: 1 proxy repository serves a version the moment it is published upstream.
insight.age-policy-off.title: Proxies without a release-age cooldown
insight.age-policy-off.why: Malicious or hijacked releases are usually found and pulled upstream within days. Without a cooldown, builds fetch them in the first minutes.
insight.approvals-aging.action: Decide them, or enable auto-approval of clean packages so reviewers only see what needs a human.
insight.approvals-aging.criteria: Yellow: a package approval request has been pending for more than 7 days.
insight.approvals-aging.summary: {count} package approval requests have been pending for more than 7 days.
insight.approvals-aging.summary-one: 1 package approval request has been pending for more than 7 days.
insight.approvals-aging.title: Package approvals waiting over a week
insight.approvals-aging.why: A request waiting for weeks blocks the team that asked, and pushes people towards fetching the package around forklift.
insight.auth-failures.action: Check whether these are misconfigured CI credentials or someone probing. Block the address at the edge or with the repository IP allow list if it is not yours.
insight.auth-failures.criteria: Red (high): a client was refused (401 or 403) 200 times or more in the last 24 hours. Yellow (medium): 20 times or more.
insight.auth-failures.summary: {count} clients were refused (401 or 403) at least {threshold} times in the last 24 hours.
insight.auth-failures.summary-one: 1 client was refused (401 or 403) at least {threshold} times in the last 24 hours.
insight.auth-failures.title: Clients repeatedly refused
insight.auth-failures.why: A burst of refused requests from one client is either a broken CI credential that fails builds or someone probing for valid credentials.
insight.copyleft-licenses.action: Confirm each use with legal, and deny the licenses you do not accept in the repository license policy so new versions are stopped at the door.
insight.copyleft-licenses.criteria: Yellow (medium): a stored version is under AGPL or SSPL. Yellow (low): a stored version is under GPL, EUPL or OSL.
insight.copyleft-licenses.summary: {count} stored package versions are under a strong copyleft license ({network} network copyleft such as AGPL or SSPL).
insight.copyleft-licenses.summary-one: 1 stored package version is under a strong copyleft license ({network} network copyleft such as AGPL or SSPL).
insight.copyleft-licenses.title: Strong copyleft licenses in stored packages
insight.copyleft-licenses.why: Strong copyleft can oblige you to publish your own source when you distribute (GPL, EUPL, OSL) or serve over a network (AGPL, SSPL) software that includes the package.
insight.coverage-bypass.action: Point the project's package manager config and CI at the forklift endpoints shown on its Coverage page, most recently active projects first.
insight.coverage-bypass.criteria: Yellow (medium): coverage is below 50% and a project in scope is not or only partly wired. Yellow (low): the same with coverage at 50% or more. Needs a completed coverage scan.
insight.coverage-bypass.summary: {count} of {target} GitLab projects do not fully build through forklift (coverage {percent}%), so their dependencies skip the policies and scans here.
insight.coverage-bypass.summary-one: 1 of {target} GitLab projects does not fully build through forklift (coverage {percent}%), so its dependencies skip the policies and scans here.
insight.coverage-bypass.title: Projects bypassing forklift
insight.coverage-bypass.why: A project that pulls from public registries directly skips every age, approval, vulnerability and license control in forklift, and its downloads never reach the audit log.
insight.license-policy-off.action: Enable the license policy and deny the licenses your organization does not accept.
insight.license-policy-off.criteria: Yellow: a repository whose format has license resolution has the license policy off.
insight.license-policy-off.summary: {count} repositories accept packages under any license.
insight.license-policy-off.summary-one: 1 repository accepts packages under any license.
insight.license-policy-off.title: No license policy
insight.license-policy-off.why: Without a policy nothing stops a package under an unacceptable license from entering builds. It is found later, if at all, in a legal review.
insight.locked-accounts.action: Confirm with the owner before unlocking. A lock nobody expected can mean someone is guessing the password.
insight.locked-accounts.criteria: Info: an account is locked after failed sign-ins.
insight.locked-accounts.summary: {count} accounts are locked after repeated failed sign-ins.
insight.locked-accounts.summary-one: 1 account is locked after repeated failed sign-ins.
insight.locked-accounts.title: Accounts locked by failed sign-ins
insight.locked-accounts.why: Lockouts follow repeated wrong passwords, which is also what password guessing looks like.
insight.oci-latest-tag.action: Deploy by immutable version tag or digest, and keep latest for local use only.
insight.oci-latest-tag.criteria: Yellow: a hosted OCI repository has an image tagged latest.
insight.oci-latest-tag.summary: {count} images are pushed as latest, which moves under every consumer on the next push.
insight.oci-latest-tag.summary-one: 1 image is pushed as latest, which moves under every consumer on the next push.
insight.oci-latest-tag.title: Images published under the mutable latest tag
insight.oci-latest-tag.why: latest points at whatever was pushed last, so two deployments of the same manifest can run different code and a rollback to latest does not roll back.
insight.oci-unsigned.action: Sign images in CI (cosign sign) and verify signatures at admission, so only images your pipeline built can run.
insight.oci-unsigned.criteria: Yellow: a tag in a hosted OCI repository has no cosign signature tag (sha256-<digest>.sig) for its manifest.
insight.oci-unsigned.summary: {count} image tags in hosted OCI repositories have no cosign signature tag next to them.
insight.oci-unsigned.summary-one: 1 image tag in a hosted OCI repository has no cosign signature tag next to it.
insight.oci-unsigned.title: Images without a signature
insight.oci-unsigned.why: Without a signature nothing proves an image came from your pipeline. An image pushed or swapped under the same tag by someone else runs as if it were yours.
insight.plaintext-upstream.action: Point the upstream at its https:// address.
insight.plaintext-upstream.criteria: Red (high): a proxy repository's upstream URL starts with http://.
insight.plaintext-upstream.summary: {count} proxy repositories fetch from an http:// upstream, so a network attacker can swap what gets cached.
insight.plaintext-upstream.summary-one: 1 proxy repository fetches from an http:// upstream, so a network attacker can swap what gets cached.
insight.plaintext-upstream.title: Proxies fetching over plain HTTP
insight.plaintext-upstream.why: Over plain HTTP anyone on the network path can read or replace what forklift caches, and the poisoned copy is then served to every build.
insight.policy-blocks.action: Update the dependency to an allowed version in the projects named here, so builds stop failing on it.
insight.policy-blocks.criteria: Yellow: a vulnerability or license policy blocked a package path in the last 7 days.
insight.policy-blocks.summary: {count} package paths were blocked by a vulnerability or license policy in the last 7 days.
insight.policy-blocks.summary-one: 1 package path was blocked by a vulnerability or license policy in the last 7 days.
insight.policy-blocks.title: Builds still requesting blocked packages
insight.policy-blocks.why: Each block is a build that failed because a dependency is not allowed. Until the dependency is updated the build keeps failing or someone works around the policy.
insight.public-repositories.action: Make them private unless anonymous access is intended, and restrict them by source IP when it is.
insight.public-repositories.criteria: Red (high): a hosted repository allows anonymous downloads. Yellow (medium): only proxy or group repositories do.
insight.public-repositories.summary: {count} repositories allow downloads without signing in ({hosted} hosted, holding internal artifacts).
insight.public-repositories.summary-one: 1 repository allows downloads without signing in ({hosted} hosted, holding internal artifacts).
insight.public-repositories.title: Repositories open to anonymous downloads
insight.public-repositories.why: Anyone who can reach forklift can download from these repositories without credentials. Hosted repositories hold your internal packages and images.
insight.retention-off.action: Turn on idle retention in the repository settings. The impact preview shows what would go before you save.
insight.retention-off.criteria: Yellow: a non-OCI repository without idle retention holds at least 10 artifacts not downloaded for 180 days.
insight.retention-off.summary: {count} repositories without idle retention hold {size} not downloaded for 180 days.
insight.retention-off.summary-one: 1 repository without idle retention holds {size} not downloaded for 180 days.
insight.retention-off.title: Unused artifacts kept forever
insight.retention-off.why: Artifacts nobody downloads cost storage and backups, and old vulnerable versions among them can be pulled back into a build by mistake.
insight.scan-gap.action: Check that the scanner is configured and reachable and that its backfill keeps up. Unscanned versions pass the vulnerability policy unless it blocks unscanned versions.
insight.scan-gap.criteria: Yellow: more than 20% of a repository's package versions (at least 10 versions) have no vulnerability scan.
insight.scan-gap.summary: {count} repositories have more than 20% of their package versions without a vulnerability scan.
insight.scan-gap.summary-one: 1 repository has more than 20% of its package versions without a vulnerability scan.
insight.scan-gap.title: Repositories with a vulnerability scan gap
insight.scan-gap.why: A version without a scan has no advisory data, so the vulnerability policy cannot judge it and the dashboards report it as clean by omission.
insight.stale-accounts.action: Disable accounts that are no longer needed, or remove their roles. With OIDC, check that leavers are removed from the mapped groups.
insight.stale-accounts.criteria: Yellow: an enabled, non-robot account with at least one role has not signed in for 90 days (or never, and was created over 90 days ago).
insight.stale-accounts.summary: {count} enabled accounts with a role have not signed in for 90 days.
insight.stale-accounts.summary-one: 1 enabled account with a role has not signed in for 90 days.
insight.stale-accounts.title: Dormant accounts with access
insight.stale-accounts.why: Accounts nobody uses are not watched. If their credentials leak, the access they still hold is used without anyone noticing.
insight.storage-capacity.action: Expand the PersistentVolume before it fills. To free space now, turn on idle retention for repositories holding unused artifacts and delete repositories nobody uses. The Storage page shows what the blobs take.
insight.storage-capacity.criteria: Red (critical): the volume holding the data directory is 90% full or more. Red (high): 80% or more. Yellow (medium): 70% or more.
insight.storage-capacity.summary: The data volume is {percent}% full with {free} left. Writes fail once it fills.
insight.storage-capacity.title: Data volume running out of space
insight.storage-capacity.why: The data volume holds the metadata database, and the blobs on the filesystem backend. Once it is full every upload, proxy cache fill and metadata write fails at the same time, so builds break in every repository at once.
insight.tokens-no-expiry.action: Reissue them with an expiry and rotate on a schedule. A leaked token without expiry stays valid until someone notices.
insight.tokens-no-expiry.criteria: Red (high): a token without expiry belongs to an administrator. Yellow (medium): only other accounts hold such tokens.
insight.tokens-no-expiry.summary: {count} access tokens have no expiry ({admin} owned by administrators).
insight.tokens-no-expiry.summary-one: 1 access token has no expiry ({admin} owned by administrators).
insight.tokens-no-expiry.title: Access tokens that never expire
insight.tokens-no-expiry.why: A token without expiry stays valid forever. Tokens end up in CI variables, scripts and logs, and a leaked one keeps working until someone notices.
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.action: Scope automation tokens to the repositories and actions they need, or issue them from a robot account with a narrow role.
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.criteria: Red (high): a token of an account with global admin has no scopes.
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.summary: {count} tokens of administrators carry no scopes, so each one is full admin over the API and every repository.
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.summary-on: 1 administrator token carries no scopes, so it is full admin over the API and every repository.
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.title: Administrator tokens without scopes
insight.tokens-unscoped-admin.why: An unscoped token carries all of its owner's rights. For an administrator that is full control of forklift, exercised by whatever holds the token.
insight.tokens-unused.action: Revoke them. An unused credential only adds exposure.
insight.tokens-unused.criteria: Yellow: an unexpired token has not been used for 90 days (or never, and was created over 90 days ago).
insight.tokens-unused.summary: {count} unexpired access tokens have not been used for 90 days.
insight.tokens-unused.summary-one: 1 unexpired access token has not been used for 90 days.
insight.tokens-unused.title: Valid tokens unused for 90 days
insight.tokens-unused.why: A credential nobody uses has no reason to exist, but it can still be stolen and used.
insight.unused-roles.action: Delete roles that are no longer needed, or remove them from the chart policy for managed ones. Review the grants of a role you keep before assigning it.
insight.unused-roles.criteria: Yellow (low): a role created over 7 days ago is not assigned to any user, not mapped from any OIDC group and is not the default role.
insight.unused-roles.summary: {count} roles are not assigned to any user or mapped from any group.
insight.unused-roles.summary-one: 1 role is not assigned to any user or mapped from any group.
insight.unused-roles.title: Roles nobody holds
insight.unused-roles.why: A role assigned to no one grants nothing today, but its permissions are rarely reviewed. Assigning it later hands out whatever it was once given, often more than intended.
insight.vuln-accepted.action: Review the ignore list on a schedule and remove entries whose reason no longer holds or that now have a fixed version.
insight.vuln-accepted.criteria: Info: a repository's vulnerability policy has advisory ids on its ignore list.
insight.vuln-accepted.summary: {count} repositories ignore {ignored} advisories in their vulnerability policy.
insight.vuln-accepted.summary-one: 1 repository ignores {ignored} advisories in its vulnerability policy.
insight.vuln-accepted.title: Advisories ignored by policy
insight.vuln-accepted.why: An ignored advisory is an accepted risk. Acceptances made once are rarely revisited, even after a fix ships or the advisory is upgraded.
insight.vuln-dormant.action: Delete them, or turn on idle retention so unused versions leave on their own before a build pulls them again.
insight.vuln-dormant.criteria: Yellow: a stored package version with a critical or high advisory has not been served for 30 days.
insight.vuln-dormant.summary: {count} stored package versions with critical or high advisories ({critical} critical) have not been served for 30 days.
insight.vuln-dormant.summary-one: 1 stored package version with a critical or high advisory ({critical} critical) has not been served for 30 days.
insight.vuln-dormant.title: Vulnerable versions stored but unused
insight.vuln-dormant.why: Unused vulnerable versions do no harm until a lockfile, a rollback or a forgotten branch pulls them again, and then they arrive without anyone re-checking them. They also occupy storage.
insight.vuln-in-use.action: Upgrade consumers to a fixed version, then block the vulnerable versions with a version deny or a vulnerability policy set to block.
insight.vuln-in-use.criteria: Red (critical): a stored package version with a critical advisory was served in the last 30 days. Red (high): the same with a high advisory and no critical one.
insight.vuln-in-use.summary: {count} package versions with critical or high advisories ({critical} critical) were served in the last 30 days.
insight.vuln-in-use.summary-one: 1 package version with a critical or high advisory ({critical} critical) was served in the last 30 days.
insight.vuln-in-use.title: Vulnerable versions still being downloaded
insight.vuln-in-use.why: Builds that download these versions ship code with known, often exploitable flaws into your services. A version served this month is in active use, so this is the shortest path from a published advisory to an incident.
insight.vuln-moderate.action: Pick them up in routine dependency updates, starting with the most downloaded packages.
insight.vuln-moderate.criteria: Yellow (low): a stored package version whose worst advisory is medium or low was served in the last 30 days.
insight.vuln-moderate.summary: {count} package versions with medium or low advisories were served in the last 30 days.
insight.vuln-moderate.summary-one: 1 package version with a medium or low advisory was served in the last 30 days.
insight.vuln-moderate.title: Versions with medium or low advisories in use
insight.vuln-moderate.why: Medium and low advisories are rarely urgent alone, but they pile up, get chained with others, and are cheapest to fix while the upgrade is small.
insight.vuln-policy-off.action: Enable the vulnerability policy with action block (or warn first) at threshold high.
insight.vuln-policy-off.criteria: Yellow: a repository whose format has vulnerability scanning has the vulnerability policy off, or on with action audit.
insight.vuln-policy-off.summary: {count} repositories serve known-vulnerable versions without warning or blocking.
insight.vuln-policy-off.summary-one: 1 repository serves known-vulnerable versions without warning or blocking.
insight.vuln-policy-off.title: Vulnerability policy not enforcing
insight.vuln-policy-off.why: With the policy off or audit-only, a version with a known critical advisory is served like any other, and nobody is told at install time.
insight.vuln-widespread.action: Deny the affected versions in the vulnerability policy or a version deny, and announce the fixed version to the teams that pull it.
insight.vuln-widespread.criteria: Yellow (medium): a high advisory affects 3 or more stored versions. Red (high): the same for a critical advisory.
insight.vuln-widespread.summary: {count} critical or high advisories ({critical} critical) each affect {min} or more stored versions.
insight.vuln-widespread.summary-one: 1 critical or high advisory ({critical} critical) affects {min} or more stored versions.
insight.vuln-widespread.title: Advisories spread across many versions
insight.vuln-widespread.why: One advisory present in many stored versions means many teams depend on the affected package. Fixing it centrally, with one deny rule or one shared upgrade, removes the exposure everywhere at once.
insights.ack-by: By {user} on {at}, until {until}. Flagged when acknowledged: {flagged}.
insights.ack-expired: Acknowledgement expired on {date}; the check counts again
insights.ack-help: Acknowledge this check if the risk is accepted or being handled. It returns on its own when the period ends or new items appear.
insights.ack-new-items: {count} new items since it was acknowledged; the check counts again
insights.ack-note-placeholder: Why it is accepted, or who is fixing it and by when
insights.ack-state-active: Acknowledged. The check is left out of the score, the counts and alarms.
insights.ack-state-expired: The acknowledgement expired, so the check counts again.
insights.ack-state-new_items: The check flags more items than when it was acknowledged, so it counts again.
insights.all-clear: Nothing to improve. Every rule passed on the last analysis.
insights.category-desc-exposure: Who and what can reach forklift's content.
insights.category-desc-operations: Day-to-day hygiene that keeps the controls effective.
insights.category-desc-policy: The controls configured on each repository.
insights.category-desc-supply-chain: What enters your builds: packages, images and where they come from.
insights.check-missing: This check is not in the latest analysis, or you cannot see it.
insights.check-restricted: Check details are available to administrators, auditors and security reviewers.
insights.description: Forklift analyzes every repository, artifact, image, account, token and the recent audit log on a schedule, and turns them into ranked improvements for DevOps engineers and SREs, security engineers and developers.
insights.history-drag-hint: Drag across a chart to zoom in
insights.no-report: No analysis has run yet. The first one starts when the leader comes up and then runs on its schedule.
insights.result-ok: No problems detected in the latest analysis.
insights.result-unavailable: The check could not run: it needs data that is not there yet, such as a completed coverage scan.
insights.scope-repositories: You see the checks and their status for the repositories you can read, plus Forklift coverage. Opening a check, and account and token checks, are for administrators, auditors and security reviewers.
insights.settings-alarm-hint: Sends the latest analysis to a notification receiver on a schedule. Send alarm on the Insights page still sends one on demand.
insights.settings-description: When the analysis runs and when its alarm goes out. Changes take effect within a minute.
insights.settings-interval-hint: How long after the last analysis the next one runs, from 5 to 1440 minutes. Each run reads every artifact, so keep it at an hour or more on a large instance.
insights.settings-min-severity-hint: The alarm goes out only while an open finding is at least this severe. Acknowledged checks do not count.
insights.settings-preview-empty: Nothing analyzed yet, so there is no alarm to preview. Run the analysis from the Security tab first.
insights.settings-receiver-hint: The alarm is posted to this receiver's webhook.
insights.settings-send-report: Send the alarm on a schedule
insights.settings-skip-unchanged-hint: Holds the alarm back unless a check is newly flagged or flags more items than at the last scheduled alarm.
insights.settings-unavailable: Settings are unavailable. They need administrator or security permission.
insights.summary-scoped: {count} affected in the repositories you can read.
insights.summary-scoped-one: 1 item affected in the repositories you can read.
insights.title: Security Insights
label.invalid: A label must be a key or key:value of letters, digits, - and _ (max 64 characters).
login.access-note: Access is limited by your assigned role.
login.description: Manage repository policies, approvals, and scoped tokens.
login.title: Sign in to forklift
notification.delete-blocked: Detach this receiver from every repository before deleting it.
notification.delete-confirm: Repositories selecting this receiver will stop notifying it. This cannot be undone.
notification.description: A receiver is a webhook (Slack/Mattermost-compatible) alerted when a package enters a repository's approval queue. Each repository chooses which receivers to notify in its Settings.
notification.empty: No receivers yet. Add one to start sending approval alarms.
notification.linked-repos-hint: Repositories that send approval alarms through this receiver.
notification.subtitle: · alarm channels
notification.title: Notifications
notification.webhook-note: The webhook URL is never shown again after it is saved. Leave it blank when editing to keep the current URL.
notification.webhook-warning: The webhook URL cannot be viewed again after you save it. You can only replace it with a new one. Keep a copy somewhere safe before you save.
oci.delete-help: The selected images are deleted together with every tag pointing at them, other tags of the same image included. Layers no remaining image uses are reclaimed by the next prune after a 24 hour grace. A proxy can cache them again on the next pull, hosted pushes cannot be recovered.
oci.no-images: No tagged images yet. Push with docker or helm or oras.
quota.access-tokens-desc: Maximum number of personal access tokens this user can hold.
quota.hard-limit-desc: A fixed limit that cannot be changed.
quota.login-failures-desc: Consecutive failed password logins. The account locks when the hard limit is reached.
quota.login-failures-robot-desc: Robot accounts are token-only and cannot log in interactively so this quota does not apply.
quota.name: Quota name
quota.soft-limit-desc: A default limit that an administrator can adjust.
quota.title: Quotas
repo.acl-behavior-detail: When enabled, only requests from a matching source IP are served; others receive 403. An empty allow list blocks every request.
repo.allow-licenses: Allow licenses (SPDX id, one per line; empty = allow all but denied)
repo.approval-audit: Package approval is in audit mode. Requests are logged but packages are still served.
repo.approval-on: Package approval is on. An admin must approve a package before this proxy serves it.
repo.approvers-subtitle: · users who can approve this repository
repo.artifact-unavailable: Artifact file is missing from storage.
repo.artifact-unavailable-hosted: Downloads and installs of this artifact fail. Publish this version again to restore it, or ask an administrator.
repo.artifact-unavailable-proxy: Requests for this artifact fail. Delete the cached entry so it is fetched from the upstream again.
repo.auto-approve-clean-desc: Admit a package automatically once its vulnerability scan comes back with no advisories. Requires a scanner; vulnerable and not-yet-scanned packages still await review.
repo.basics-description: Choose the protocol and serving mode. The generated endpoint follows this selection.
repo.block-unresolved: Block versions not yet resolved (block action only)
repo.block-unscanned: Block versions not yet scanned (block action only)
repo.bulk-delete-denied: Deleting artifacts needs admin on this repository.
repo.bulk-delete-help: The selected artifacts are removed from this repository. A proxy can re-cache them on the next request; hosted uploads cannot be recovered.
repo.bulk-label-denied: Labelling needs admin on this repository, or having uploaded the artifact.
repo.bulk-label-help: The label is applied to every selected artifact. Artifacts you may not label are skipped and listed afterwards.
repo.bulk-remove-label-none: None of the selected artifacts carry a label.
repo.bulk-row-denied: Not yours to label or delete. Labelling needs admin on this repository, or having uploaded the artifact.
repo.bulk-select-page: Select every artifact on this page
repo.cooldown-label: Block versions newer than a cooldown window
repo.cooldown-note: Use this when newly published packages should cool down before serving.
repo.delete-confirm: This removes the repository and its cached/hosted artifacts. This cannot be undone.
repo.delete-note: Deleting a repository removes its cached/hosted artifacts. This cannot be undone.
repo.delete-seeded-note: This is a predefined repository, seeded when Forklift first started. It is kept so the default repository layout stays intact, and it would be recreated on the next startup if removed. It cannot be deleted by anyone, including administrators.
repo.deny-licenses: Deny licenses (SPDX id, one per line)
repo.description-hint: Optional free text shown in the repository list and detail pages.
repo.downloads-30d-help: Successful GET requests recorded in the last 30 days (includes partial responses). Limited to retained audit history and requests to this repository; group requests are excluded.
repo.filter-sampled: Among the 500 most recently accessed artifacts, like the Statistics tab
repo.force-delete-help: will be removed. Its bytes are already missing from storage, so nothing further is lost, and the version can be published again afterwards. This cannot be undone.
repo.idle-days-help: Counted from the last download (OCI: last push or pull).
repo.idle-days-invalid: Enter at least 1 day, or turn retention off.
repo.last-accessed-by-help: Last recorded authenticated user. Anonymous requests do not replace this value.
repo.license-gate: Gate packages by their declared license
repo.license-note: Licenses are resolved per version from deps.dev. A denied license, or any license outside a non-empty allow list, triggers the selected action. Matching is case-insensitive.
repo.list-description: Host and proxy artifacts across Maven, npm, Cargo, Go, and PyPI. Configure per-repository caching and supply-chain policies (age cooldown, package approval).
repo.members-note: Select member repositories in lookup order. The first hit wins.
repo.new-description: Register a hosted, proxy, or group repository for package delivery.
repo.no-access-role: No role grants access to this repository. Add a permission on a role (Roles page) whose pattern matches this repository.
repo.no-access-token: No access token reaches this repository.
repo.no-cached-artifacts: No cached artifacts yet. Pull through the endpoint above to populate the cache.
repo.offline-note: This repository is offline: uploads and downloads are refused (503). Its config and artifacts are kept.
repo.online-note: This repository is online and serving the package protocols.
repo.policy-order-desc-2: and audit gates only log and let it continue.
repo.proxy-description: Configure the remote registry and optional supply-chain cooldown.
repo.public-access-note: Making this repository public allows anyone to download its artifacts without signing in. Uploads and deletes still require authentication.
repo.purge-confirm: This removes every cached or hosted artifact in the repository. The repository and its settings stay. A proxy will re-cache on demand; hosted uploads cannot be recovered.
repo.purge-note: Purging removes all cached/hosted artifacts but keeps the repository and its settings. This cannot be undone.
repo.pypi-legacy-zip-help: Disabled by default. ZIP archives still require one safe project-version root and matching PKG-INFO metadata.
repo.quarantine-desc: · alarm a receiver when a package is quarantined
repo.readonly-note: Read-only view. You can review the configuration but not change it.
repo.receivers-note: Selected receivers get a webhook alarm when a package here enters the approval queue. Manage receivers on the Notifications page.
repo.require-approval: Require approval before serving a package
repo.restrict-by-ip: Restrict access by client source IP
repo.retention-badge-tip: Auto-deletes artifacts not downloaded for {days} days.
repo.retention-badge-tip-one: Auto-deletes artifacts not downloaded for {days} day.
repo.retention-note: Artifacts not downloaded for this many days are deleted automatically, checked every hour. Each removal is recorded in the audit log. Based on the last download time.
repo.retention-note-oci: Tags neither pushed nor pulled for this many days are removed automatically, checked every hour, and the unreferenced manifests and layers are reclaimed after that. Signature and SBOM tags follow their image. Each removal is recorded in the audit log.
repo.retention-on: Delete artifacts that are not downloaded
repo.retention-preview-count: {count} artifacts ({size}) would be deleted on the next hourly pass with this setting.
repo.retention-preview-count-oci: {count} tags would be removed on the next hourly pass with this setting. Layers still used by other tags stay.
repo.retention-preview-count-oci-one: {count} tag would be removed on the next hourly pass with this setting. Layers still used by other tags stay.
repo.retention-preview-count-one: {count} artifact ({size}) would be deleted on the next hourly pass with this setting.
repo.retention-preview-more: and {count} more, least recently used first.
repo.retention-preview-none: Nothing matches now. No artifact would be deleted on the next pass.
repo.retention-preview-none-oci: Nothing matches now. No tag would be removed on the next pass.
repo.security-controls-group-desc: Access control is enforced at the group entry point; artifact policies run on the member that serves the request.
repo.security-controls-hosted-desc: Access control, security scans, version denies, and approval quarantine are enforced for hosted artifacts.
repo.security-controls-proxy-desc: Access and artifact guards are fixed. Automated assessments run in the configured order, and human approval remains final.
repo.stat-all-clean: All scanned artifacts are clean, no advisories.
repo.stat-none-scanned: No artifacts have been scanned yet.
repo.type.group-desc: Combine repositories behind a single read-only URL
repo.type.hosted-desc: Store artifacts uploaded directly by your team
repo.type.proxy-desc: Cache and serve artifacts from an upstream registry
repo.upload-approval-notice: Uploads to this repository are quarantined and only served after a reviewer approves the package.
repo.upload-complete: Upload complete. Security scans have been queued.
repo.upload-description: Choose a file and Forklift derives the repository path for you, validating the coordinate and collision before any bytes are uploaded.
repo.upload-exists: Validation failed: this path already exists.
repo.upload-fields-auto: Derived from the file you chose. Adjust if needed.
repo.upload-pending: Upload complete and quarantined. The artifact will be served after approval.
repo.upstream-auth-desc: Authenticate requests to a private upstream. Public registries do not require this.
repo.upstream-auth-note: Credentials are stored server side and always shown masked. Leave a masked value untouched to keep the stored secret; type a new value to replace it.
repo.version-deny-detail: Explicitly blocked versions are always checked in the Artifact guard stage.
repo.visibility-private-desc: Downloads require a signed-in account or an access token.
repo.visibility-public-desc: Anyone can download artifacts without signing in. Uploads still require authentication.
role.action-admin: Full control of the repository including settings and upstream credentials.
role.action-approve: Approve or reject package approval requests.
role.action-audit: Read audit logs and administrative pages.
role.action-read: Download artifacts and browse the repository.
role.action-security: Edit repository security policies such as approval, vulnerability and license rules.
role.delete-confirm: Users and group mappings holding this role lose its permissions immediately. This cannot be undone.
role.empty: No roles yet. Create one to grant repository access.
role.list-description: Bundle repository permissions (read, write, delete, approve, audit, security, admin) over name patterns. Open a role to map permissions; roles are assigned to users on each user's detail page.
role.managed-note: This role was configured by a Forklift administrator in the declarative RBAC policy so it cannot be edited here. To change its permissions or delete it ask an administrator to update the policy file and restart forklift.
role.new-description: Define a reusable access profile and optional repository permissions.
role.no-users: No users have this role. Assign it from a user's detail page.
role.permissions-description: Add repository patterns and allowed actions. Wildcards are accepted.
search.type-to-search: Type at least 2 characters to search.
settings.appearance-description: Choose a fixed theme or follow your operating system setting.
settings.card-description: These settings apply only to the current browser.
settings.content-width-description: The default content width for the console. Wide uses the available width on table views.
settings.description: Preferences are saved in this browser until account-level settings are available.
settings.language-description: Store the preferred interface language for this browser.
settings.language.en-description: Use English as the preferred UI language.
settings.language.ko-description: Use Korean as the preferred UI language.
settings.title: Settings
storage.conditional-writes-ignored: This object store does not enforce S3 conditional writes, so HA mode cannot be enabled
storage.consistency-see-statistics: Open the repository Statistics tab for detail
storage.description: Storage backend health and usage at a glance. Object stores with an admin API (MinIO, RustFS, SeaweedFS, Garage) also show live cluster capacity and storage-unit status.
storage.fs-note: This instance uses the filesystem backend. Cluster metrics are available only with an object-storage backend whose provider has an admin API.
storage.migration-json-hint: The full record, including the report location.
storage.migration-stored-at-description: The object this report is read from.
storage.migrations-description: Every forklift migrate-storage run recorded in this store, succeeded, failed or dry. Open a run for its full report.
storage.migrations-empty: No migration has been recorded in this store.
storage.title: Storage
storage.usage-cluster-other-hint: Objects other clients keep in this store, such as other buckets
storage.usage-cluster-rest-hint: This store does not report its object bytes, so other clients' objects and system data cannot be told apart
storage.usage-forklift-other-hint: Smaller formats and blobs awaiting cleanup
storage.usage-system-hint: Disk space outside object data: replicas or parity, deleted space not yet reclaimed, store metadata and other files on the same disks
token.copy-warning: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again.
token.description-placeholder: What this token is used for
token.edit-permissions-note: Add or revoke repository permissions. The token secret stays the same.
token.expiry-note: Tokens expire after at most one year.
token.hard-limit: This limit is fixed and cannot be changed.
token.help-1: Scoped credentials for package clients, limited to chosen repositories and actions within your own permissions. Use a token as the password in your package manager (npm
token.incomplete-note: Complete all required fields before creating a token.
token.limit-reached: Token limit reached. Revoke one to free a slot.
token.name: Token name
token.new-description: Issue a scoped access token with an expiration date and repository permissions.
token.permissions-description: Add repository patterns and allowed token actions.
token.readonly-note: Read-only: only administrators can create or revoke tokens.
token.revoke-confirm-message: Clients using this token will immediately lose access. This cannot be undone.
token.scopes-required: At least one permission is required
token.subtitle: · scoped credentials for package clients
token.title: Access tokens
upload.assets-help: Files are renamed to canonical Maven paths. Add classifiers such as sources or javadoc explicitly.
upload.assets-required: Select a file and extension for every asset.
upload.cancelled: The upload was cancelled. Select Upload artifact to start a new attempt.
upload.cargo-file-help: Select the .crate produced by cargo package.
upload.cargo-help: Forklift validates Cargo.toml and the archive root, then atomically appends the sparse-index entry.
upload.choose-file-first: Choose a file to begin. The coordinates are filled in from it automatically.
upload.classifier-invalid: Only letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen are allowed.
upload.coordinates-required: Group ID, Artifact ID, version, and packaging are required.
upload.delete-publication-help: All files owned by this publication will be removed atomically and package metadata will be rebuilt. This cannot be undone.
upload.generate-pom-help: Forklift creates a Maven 4.0.0 POM from these coordinates.
upload.go-help: Forklift validates the GOPROXY ZIP root and module directive, then creates .mod, .info, list, and @latest atomically.
upload.go-mod-help: If omitted, the ZIP go.mod is used or a minimal file is generated.
upload.go-mod-invalid: The optional module metadata file must use the .mod extension.
upload.go-private-help: For private modules, configure GOPRIVATE or GONOSUMDB for this module path.
upload.go-required: Enter a module path and canonical version, then select one module ZIP.
upload.go-zip-help: Every entry must use the exact module@version/ root.
upload.npm-file-help: Select the .tgz produced by npm pack.
upload.npm-help: Forklift reads name and version from package/package.json and atomically updates the packument.
upload.npm-tag-help: Defaults to latest. SemVer-like tags are rejected.
upload.pom-mode-conflict: Disable POM generation when an unclassified .pom asset is supplied.
upload.pom-supplied: An uploaded POM will be validated against these coordinates.
upload.publication-broken: Some files of this version are missing from storage.
upload.pypi-files-help: Select one or more wheels and at most one .tar.gz source distribution for the same release.
upload.pypi-files-required: Select supported .whl or .tar.gz files for one release.
upload.pypi-help: Name and version are read from wheel METADATA or sdist PKG-INFO. Every file must identify the same release.
upload.replace-ack: I understand that every file in this Maven publication will be replaced atomically.
upload.replace-help: Review the conflicting paths. Confirmation requires delete permission and expires after 30 minutes.
upload.title: Upload artifact
upload.unyank-tooltip: Makes this version selectable again when Cargo resolves new dependencies.
upload.yank-help: Cargo keeps the crate bytes and changes only the selected sparse-index entry. Existing lockfiles can still download a yanked version.
upload.yank-tooltip: Stops Cargo from choosing this version for new dependencies. The .crate file stays, so builds pinned by an existing Cargo.lock keep working. Unyank reverses it.
user.delete-note: Deleting a user revokes all of their tokens and role assignments. This cannot be undone.
user.delete-self-note: You cannot delete your own account.
user.impersonate-active-note: Stop your current impersonation before starting another one.
user.impersonate-disabled-note: A disabled account cannot be impersonated.
user.impersonate-modal-note: Your session is replaced by one acting as this user until you stop, or for one hour.
user.impersonate-note: Impersonating signs you in as this user with their permissions, so you see Forklift exactly as they do. Your own session is replaced until you stop impersonating, and the reason you give is written to the server log. Actions you take are recorded as this user, with your account noted alongside.
user.impersonate-reason-hint: At least 10 characters. Recorded in the server log with both usernames.
user.impersonate-reason-placeholder: e.g. reproducing the 403 reported on the npm proxy
user.impersonate-robot-note: A robot account cannot be impersonated because it cannot sign in.
user.impersonate-self-note: You are already signed in as this account.
user.initial-password-note: Set an initial password for this local account.
user.list-description: Local and OIDC accounts. Open a user to map roles, reset the password, or disable access. OIDC users appear automatically at first login.
user.locked-note: Locked after too many failed password attempts - unlock it in Account lockout.
user.lockout-note: When enabled, the account is locked after 5 consecutive failed password attempts and must be unlocked by an administrator.
user.lockout-protected-note: The default admin account cannot be locked out.
user.new-description: Create a local account and optionally assign an initial role.
user.no-role-note: A user with no role cannot access repositories until one is assigned.
user.oidc-note: OIDC users are created automatically at first login.
user.protected-note: This is the default administrator account, created when Forklift first started. Its status is locked active so the system always keeps at least one administrator who can sign in and recover access. It cannot be disabled by anyone, including other administrators.
user.robot-password-note: A robot account cannot sign in. It does not use a password. Create the account and then issue a token from its detail page for automation.
user.self-note: You are signed in as this account, so you cannot disable it yourself. This guards against accidentally locking yourself out of Forklift. If this account needs to be disabled, ask another administrator to do it.
user.status-desc-1: account can sign in to Forklift and use its credentials to pull and publish artifacts, while
user.status-desc-2: immediately revokes that access by stopping all sessions and tokens. The account, its tokens and its role assignments are preserved, so disabling is a reversible alternative to deletion that you can undo at any time by re-enabling.
user.type-robot-desc: Token-only account for automation. It cannot sign in.
user.type-user-desc: Signs in with a password or OIDC and can own tokens.
